title: Doggerland, and the Other Drowned Countries
metaTitle: Doggerland, the Land Under the North Sea - Older Than Morning
metaDescription: Doggerland and the other land now under the sea, told gently for sleep. Every claim sourced, every date given in the system its source used.
imageAlt: A low, pale shore above a still, dark sea, with a paler shape faintly visible beneath the surface
summary: Tonight is about land that is now under the sea, most of it beneath the North Sea, between Britain and the continent, and then other shelves on the far side of the world and at the edge of Arabia. There is no single date to point to. The land went under in different places at different times, and the sources do not agree on when it finished.

The evening is told through places: a sandbank far out at sea, an empty field in Yorkshire, a harbour at Rotterdam, a row of stones on the Baltic floor, and a layer of sand under a farm in Scotland. It runs from roughly 20,000 to 7,000 years ago, a frame and not a measurement. Every date is given in the system its source used, and one chapter explains why a radiocarbon year, a calendar year and a year B C are not the same ruler.

A good deal of it is unsettled: how low the sea stood, how much of the land has been mapped, when Britain became an island, whether a wave from a slide off Norway ended the last low ground, and whether a row of stones on the Baltic floor was set there or formed that way. The episode gives each figure with the name of whoever said it, and chooses none.

It stays gentle throughout. The cast is sand, clay, peat, stone, wood and water, with no animals and no people on screen, only what people left behind. It is meant for listening in the dark or while falling asleep.
